measurement_note: All 7 new-table kinds were built through ONE shared generic loader (`load_simple_kind_table` in src/rules_core/rules_tables/simple_kind_tables.rs) in a single commit (052a9182bf). Per-table wall-clock time was NOT independently measured -- there were not 7 separate build sessions to time, and inventing 7 distinct stopwatch readings for one shared implementation would fabricate precision that does not exist (AGENTS.md rule 9). What IS measured and re-derivable: (1) real commit-to-commit wall time for each cycle as a whole, (2) exact marginal lines added per kind via git/grep on the committed file, which is the real cost differentiator the spread depends on. Per-table wall time below is therefore explicitly marked ESTIMATE, pro-rated from measured marginal lines against the measured cycle wall time -- never presented as independently timed.

measured_cycle_wall_time.caveat: these are whole-cycle wall times (implementation + tests + receipt + docs for ALL kinds in that cycle together), not a per-table figure -- reported here because they are the only genuinely measured timestamps this bundle produced, per rule 9 (mark or omit, never fabricate).

spread.finding: The single most important number for pricing `power` (Epic 5) is NOT a blended average across 8 tables -- it is that per-kind marginal cost here is dominated by whether the kind's corpus directory name matches its kind name (2-line kinds) or not (trait's 12 lines), NOT by record count: `ability` (4,337 records) and `domain` (183 records) cost nearly the same (7 vs 2 marginal lines) because both reuse the same generic loader unmodified. `power`'s true cost driver for Epic 5's pricing is therefore: does `power`'s corpus shape (ultimate_psionics) match this generic per-(book,key)-record loader, or does it need its own shape handling the way `trait` did -- record count alone does not predict cost.
